page: Microsoft Azure B16s_v2 is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Bsv2 family, managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled, 48 MB of L3 cache, and 64 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The underlying architecture includes hardware support for AVX, AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic accelerators like AES and SHA-NI.

Because the B16s_v2 utilizes a burstable CPU credit mechanism, baseline performance is tailored for variable workloads rather than continuous maximum compute loads. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits middle-tier, average performance across compute, memory, and data processing tests. It achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 9,893.0 and a single-core score of 1,645.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 21,253.65. Synthetic Redis benchmarks delivered 15.86 million SET operations per second, while uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 97.68 GB/sec.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators like GPUs, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage for persistent file systems. This architecture delivers balanced resource density and cost efficiency for sporadic usage patterns where constant peak utilization is unnecessary. The B16s_v2 is suitable for staging environments, development servers, moderate-traffic web serving, microservices backends, and intermittent build or CI/CD pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure B16s_v2 is a general-purpose, burstable cloud virtual machine based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. Provisioned with 16 vCPUs, 8 physical cores with hyper-threading, and 64 GB of RAM, the instance maintains a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration. It features 48 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, but excludes integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing remote storage volumes instead. Benchmark measurements position the instance squarely within the average middle-tier tier across CPU, memory bandwidth, and operational tests, highlighted by 15.86 million Redis SET operations per second and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 9,893.0. By employing a burstable compute model, the instance offers cost-efficient utilization for non-continuous, variable workloads. It is functionally suited for intermediate development clusters, code compilation, static web serving, background queue handlers, and build automation environments.
